correctness.rationale: The proof gives an if-and-only-if Pfaffian criterion for smooth quadrics over characteristic two. Exhaustive enumeration of all 1,024 forms, the 448 smooth forms and every eligible two-dimensional subspace yields exactly 14,336 all-smooth pencils; independent polar enumeration gives 56*256=14,336. The 12 elementary transvections generate all PGL4(F2) and give precisely five disjoint orbit sizes 560, 3360, 5040, 5040 and 336, with base rational cardinalities 6, 6, 2, 4 and 0. Explicit four-element stabilizer certificates establish the Klein-four and cyclic-four types for the two smooth-base representatives. For both 5040-orbit representatives, the Jacobian-ideal Groebner basis is [1] in each of four affine charts, proving geometric smoothness of their complete-intersection bases. A smooth genus-one curve over F2 has 1..5 points by the Hasse bound; the other orbits with 0 or 6 base points are singular. Frobenius traces are 3-N and direct F4/F8 point counts independently confirm the elliptic formulas. The included verifier was executed successfully and returned BINARY_QUADRIC_PENCIL_SMOOTH_BASE_ORBITS_PASS 14336 5 5040 5040 10080. Exact computational checks are proofs of these finite enumerations, not extrapolations.

originality.rationale: The 2022 primary source constructs smooth pencils in characteristic two, but its inspected Section 3 does not give a complete count or rational-projective classification of those with geometrically smooth complete-intersection bases. The 1988 Bruen-Hirschfeld abstract explicitly limits its classification to non-absolutely-irreducible bases, outside the present genus-one smooth-base sector; full text remained inaccessible and is recorded as a historical risk, not certified noncoverage. The characteristic-zero pencil classification does not imply an F2 census. Exact searches for 5040/10080-orbit formulas and elliptic-quartic pencils identified no decisive equivalent table. Negative searches alone have not been treated as proof of priority. The new claim is the precise two-orbit smooth-base classification, not generic existence or previously studied singular-base orbit descriptions.

value.rationale: This resolves a natural small-field classification motivated by published existence of rational pencils whose every member is smooth. A smooth intersection of two quadrics is an essential genus-one model, and it is a substantive geometric question which of these pencils have a smooth common elliptic quartic, and how their rational projective equivalence classes distribute. Exactly two 5040-sized orbits distinguish different Frobenius traces, isogeny classes and stabilizer group isomorphism types, providing genuine structural information beyond existence and beyond non-absolutely-irreducible base classifications. The finite object and invariant are mathematically intrinsic and complete, not a coefficient slice or arbitrary parameter test. The result is deliberately limited to the full natural F2 domain; no general-field theorem is claimed.
